title: User-Managed Access 2.0
heading: User-Managed Access 2.0
lead: A resource owner decides ahead of time who may reach the resources a resource server holds for them, and a requesting party obtains a token for them from this authorization server. Every permission is a question put to the XACML engine; nothing is decided in code.
on: User-Managed Access is on in this realm.
off: User-Managed Access is off in this realm (uma.enabled); these endpoints answer 501.
noObject: This realm has no sts-uma-protection-api object, so the protection API is off here.
rreg: Registers, lists, reads, updates and deletes the resources a resource server holds for an owner.
perm: Issues one permission ticket for one or several permissions.
discovery: Describes this authorization server's UMA endpoints.
claims: Signs a requesting party in and gathers claims about them.
pat: Both protection API endpoints take a protection API token: an access token of this realm, audienced to its /uma and carrying {scope}. Its subject is the owner of everything registered with it.
layerRealm: The realm's uma-authorization policy: which resource servers, clients and claim issuers may take part, and that a requesting party is known.
layerOwner: The resource owner's own document, written by a form on the portal.
layerFga: The resource server's fine-grained policy, where it enforces one.
layerGate: The issuance gate, as for every access token.
absence: Every layer must permit. An owner with no document shares nothing: absence is never consent.
noServers: No application is declared for uma in this realm.
grantPending: The uma-ticket grant is not performed yet, so no requesting party token is issued.
